verdictSummary: The slice proves what it says it proves. The flag-free claim is verified in code and behaviourally, the OS-level restart is real (killed process, awaited exit, changed pid, ledger continuity as the fresh-log detector), and the drive is falsifiable - the marker mutation was reproduced in this session and fails on the control assertion with the exact 409 the receipt names. Two gaps are named rather than blocking: the 'replica' is a second server process on the SAME file, not design.md's grant/socket replica, and 'scoped' is proven for exactly one seat (gm). No code edits required; two receipt-text corrections are required for accuracy.

namedGaps.gap: The 'replica' is a second server process on the SAME database file, which is NOT what design.md means by a replica.
designEvidence: openspec/changes/design-campaign-authority-and-sync/design.md:19-20 (D2) - a replica carries `authority: { role: 'replica', sourceInstanceId, grantId, scopes, revokedAt? }`, hard-guards local mutation and FORWARDS intents
design.md:31 (D3) - a replica CONNECTS to the source's /api/multiplayer/socket presenting {campaignId, grantId, token, cursor} and receives backfill then live events
design.md:34 (D4) - the replica device's server stores received events in its OWN local journal under streamType 'campaign-replica', streamId '<campaignId>#<grantId>'
design.md:11 - 'durable replicas on consuming devices (each downstream device has its own kind of server)'
namedGaps.whatIsActuallyProven: Two OS processes reading and writing one durable store converge, because the read path derives from the committed journal on every request rather than from process-local memory. That falsifies a real failure mode (a feed served from an in-process cache would NOT converge) and it is a genuine durability property. It is not replication, and the slice does not claim it is - the spec's NOT-DRIVEN footer at spec:466-469 says separate-file replication belongs to campaign-two-device-drive.spec.ts. The acceptance line says 'two-process scoped convergence', which is what was built; a reader who maps 'two-process' onto design.md's source/replica pair would be over-reading it.
namedGaps.recommendation: Owner note only. If cutover acceptance is meant to cover design.md's replica, that is a separate drive (socket + grant + campaign-replica stream), not an amendment to this one.

namedGaps.gap: 'Scoped' is proven for exactly ONE seat. Every /activity read in the drive uses the same GM participant (spec:247-260, :342-358, :424-440 all pass host.playerId).
namedGaps.evidence: src/lib/campaign/activity/campaignActivityProjection.ts:63-71,134,189,222 - the projection takes a `seesGmPrivateDetail` capability and varies the row text on it. That branch is never exercised: no second seat is bound, and no non-participant 403 is driven either (src/pages-modules/api/campaignActivityRoute.ts:94-97).
namedGaps.whatThatMeans: The drive proves the feed is SEAT-RESOLVED (the durable membership row decides viewerSeat, and both processes resolve it identically from the file). It does not prove the feed is SCOPE-FILTERED differently for different seats.
namedGaps.recommendation: A cheap follow-up row on this same spec: bind a second non-GM participant and assert (a) their feed differs where seesGmPrivateDetail applies and (b) a stranger gets 403. Not a blocker for this slice.

axis3_fourMeasuredFindings.whyItIsWorthAnOwnerNote: src/lib/campaign/authority/campaignLaunchHead.ts:24-28 states the premise in a comment: 'A campaign with no effective branch is NOT an error... While the cutover flag is off no campaign has a journal stream, so no-authoritative-stream is the ordinary answer and the launch acts on it by proceeding ungated.' CO3 measured that premise false on BOTH halves. (1) With the flag off, a co-op-hosted campaign DOES have a journal stream (spec:243 asserts head 0). (2) After the cutover the campaign is genuinely on journal authority and /head STILL answers no-authoritative-stream, so the launch gate proceeds ungated for a campaign under journal authority - the exact condition the gate exists to catch. The receipt's own open question calls this 'worth an owner look'; on the code reading it is firmer than that: the comment's stated justification no longer holds, so the ungated launch is now unjustified rather than merely undecided.

axis3_fourMeasuredFindings.recommendedOwnerNote: Before CAMPAIGN_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY_ENABLED flips, decide whether the cutover writes a branch record (making /head answer for journal-authority campaigns) or whether the launch gate should read the journal head instead of the branch head. Until then a client asking /head cannot distinguish a pre-cutover campaign from a cut-over one, and campaignLaunchHead.ts:24-28's rationale comment is stale.

axis5_caps.couldTheTwoHelpersHaveBeenONE: NO. campaignJournalTwoProcess.ts (359) + campaignJournalDrive.ts (154) = 513 lines, which breaches the 500-line cap. That specific merge is arithmetically impossible, so the question as posed answers itself.
axis5_caps.isTheFOURWaySplitAHARNESSFLOOR: Not exactly - the arithmetic floor is THREE commits (ceil(1232/500) = 3), and a legal 3-way split exists: CLI+drive (396), twoProcess (359), spec (476). So the four-way split is ONE commit above the cap-imposed floor. I judge the extra split justified on coherence rather than required by the cap: the CLI is a scripts/ deliverable with its own .gitignore allowlist line and its own runtime (tsx), while campaignJournalDrive.ts is e2e HTTP shaping - bundling them would put two unrelated concerns behind one message. The commit messages are unusually substantive and each one argues for exactly one decision, which is the behaviour the caps are meant to produce. No edit requested.

packagingRecommendation.recommendation: ONE PR carrying all four commits.
rationale: The four files form one deliverable with a single dependency chain: the spec imports both helpers, and campaignJournalTwoProcess.ts invokes the CLI. No commit is independently useful.
Two stacked PRs would necessarily produce a first PR that merges dead code - helpers and a CLI with no caller - which is worse for review and for bisect than four coherent commits behind one merge.
Every commit is independently within the node's caps (<=2 files, <=476 lines), so the cap argument for splitting the PR does not apply; the caps are already satisfied at commit granularity.
merge-tree against origin/main (9624b38f9) is clean with zero conflicts, so there is no rebase risk that a stack would de-risk.

The commit messages are the review artefact here - each one argues one decision. Keeping them as four commits under one PR preserves that; merge with --merge, not --squash, so the four messages survive.

acceptanceLineStatement.clause_noE2EOnlyFlagAsProductionProof: SATISFIED, and satisfied at the strongest tier available. The production constant is false (JournalCampaignEventStore.ts:84), the e2e arm is absent from the runner env, absent from the object handed to spawn, and absent from the replica (playwright.config.ts:318-321 forwards it only when the parent already carries it). It is asserted three ways: structurally on the spawn env (spec:184,447), read out of a real Node process that loaded the production modules (spec:143-145,444-445), and behaviourally - after create there is neither a marker nor a journal stream (spec:169,173), which only holds while both doors are shut.
acceptanceLineStatement.clause_realDurableSourceRestart: SATISFIED. A genuinely separate OS process is killed, its exit awaited, and a new process spawned on the same port against the same file; the pid change is asserted at two levels, and survival is proven on three independent surfaces plus a ledger-continuity assertion that discriminates survival from a plausible-looking fresh log.
acceptanceLineStatement.clause_twoProcessScopedConvergence: SATISFIED AS LITERALLY WORDED, with two caveats that should be recorded rather than waved past: (1) the two processes share one database file, so what is proven is that the scoped read derives from the durable record on every request rather than from process-local state - NOT design.md's grant/socket replica across separate files (design.md:19-20,31,34); (2) 'scoped' is proven as seat-RESOLVED for a single GM seat, not as scope-FILTERED across differing seats (campaignActivityProjection.ts:63-71 seesGmPrivateDetail never varies in the drive).
acceptanceLineStatement.explicitStatement: At the tier reachable WITHOUT the owner-gated flag flip, the acceptance line is SATISFIED. This slice demonstrates that once a campaign's durable marker says 'journal', the production seat gate, authority resolver, command pipeline and scoped read behave correctly across two OS processes and an OS-level restart, with no E2E-only branch anywhere in the proof. What it does NOT and CANNOT demonstrate at this tier is that any shipped code path puts a production campaign into that marker state - that is the cutover itself, and it stays off by a hardcoded constant. The remaining owner-gated work before cutover acceptance is therefore: the flag flip, the shadow-parity route to 'journal' (untouched here), the rollback-refused row (base predates #1740), the single-player seat decision (#29), and F1's /head divergence.
